question.text: An inductor of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mH</mi></math>, a capacitor of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μF</mi></math> and resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> are connected in series with a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> ac source. If the current is in phase with the emf, the amplitude of current of the circuit is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is-

solution.text:
Here, emf and current are in phase, so the circuit is either pure resistive circuit or case of resonance,

XL=XC

Thus, the impedance of circuit is  Z=R2+XL-XC2=R=20 Ω

Now, rms value of current is irms=22020=11 A

Using the relation between peak and rms value of current, we have peak value i0=irms2=112=242 A.

Hence, the value of x=242.
